_comment: The single place any scanner finding may be suppressed. Every entry needs
fails CI on an expired or unjustified entry, and generates the scanners'
ignore files from this record so there is no second place to look.
There are deliberately no trivy-image entries. The image scan runs with
--ignore-unfixed, so a finding with no published patch does not need an
entry here; a trivy-image entry is for a FIXABLE vulnerability granted a
documented, expiring grace period, which should be rare and short.

exceptions.reason: Historical example has an empty MARKET_DATA_DB_API_KEY; the adjacent numeric flush interval created a multiline generic-key false positive. No credential was committed at this location.

Role should not have access to pods/exec. The algot-data-backfill-operator Role grants create on pods/exec. The escalation path the check warns about, exec into a pod whose ServiceAccount holds higher RBAC permissions, does not exist here, and the precondition is enforced rather than assumed: every pod and every ServiceAccount in algot-data sets automountServiceAccountToken false, so a shell obtained through exec holds no Kubernetes API token at all, and validate-k8s-security.py fails the build if a pod ever runs with a mounted default token or a Role gains wildcard verbs, escalate/bind/impersonate, or read access to Secrets. The containers reached are non-root with a read-only root filesystem and ALL capabilities dropped. pods/exec is required by run-backfill.sh, run-database-integration-tests.sh, verify-deployment.sh, verify-network-policies.sh and assert-data-protection.sh, which read state from inside the database container; removing it would mean exposing the database or adding a privileged sidecar.
